newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end slightly firmer, but cash bonds weaker.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end slightly firmer, but cash bonds weaker.

text.p: Key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures closed slightly firmer on Thursday while long-term cash bonds were weaker.
"It seems that those who were selling cash bonds were covering their short positions in futures," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit.

A late fall in Tokyo stocks gave support to the market. JGBs were more solidly underpinned than many had expected after the Bank of Japan (BOJ) refrained from conducting an outright bond buying operation this morning, traders said.
The June was up 0.06 at 127.09 in a turnover of 45,122.
Many operators had expected the BOJ to buy 100 billion yen of JGBs outright at 10.10 a.m. (0110 GMT) today.

"The market is gradually factoring in the possibility that the amount of the BOJ's outright bond buying may be reduced to 100 billion yen a month from the current 200 billion yen," said a dealer at a long-term credit bank's securities unit.

Stocks were earlier boosted by news that Nippon Credit Bank and Bankers Trust New York Corp had agreed on a business alliance. NCB said on Thursday it would also consider a capital tie-up with the U.S. bank.
NCB shares ended up 22 yen at 190. The shares were bid-only throughout the day until finally trading for the first time at 218 yen just 20 minutes before the Tokyo bourse closed.
"JGBs were pressured earlier in the day by the NCB-Bankers news and the yen's weakness," said a brokerage house trader.

"However, shares of other major banks fell across the board by the end of the day, so flight-to-quality interest in JGBs stemming from worries about Japan's financial system is likely to remain intact," he added.
The dollar rose as high as 127.16 yen in Tokyo on Thursday morning, its highest level since August 1992.
Japan's private-sector machinery orders for February released in the afternoon were better than expected, but the impact on JGBs was limited, traders said.
Orders, excluding those for machinery at electric power firms and for ships, fell a seasonally-adjusted 1.6 percent month-on-month in February, after an increase of 11.8 percent in January.

"The market had expected orders to fall about four or five percent in February. However, selling that emerged after the data release was easily absorbed by short-covering," said the brokerage house trader.
The massive amount of new corporate straight bonds launched this week was partly responsible for making the upside of JGBs heavy, traders said.
So far this week, more than 300 billion yen worth of straight bonds has been launched, in addition to a 20-year JGB offering, traders said.

No significant investor activity was detected in the cash JGB market, traders said. The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.145 percent as of 4.40 p.m. (0740 GMT), up from 2.115 percent on Wednesday.
